name: Baikal Deep Underwater Neutrino Telescope

operator_text.value: Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences (INR RAS)
operator_text.quote: Baikal Neutrino Observatory INR RAS - main facilities
operator_text.note: Page is published by INR RAS, whose site describes the observatory as its own; the JINR Dubna laboratory is also a lead partner in the Baikal-GVD collaboration per the CERN Courier account, but only INR RAS is named on the official facility page fetched.

intervals.label: project origin
intervals.quote: The start of the Baikal neutrino experiment dates back to 1 October 1980, when a laboratory of high-energy neutrino astrophysics was established at the Institute for Nuclear Research of the former Academy of Sciences of the USSR in Moscow
intervals.note: Covers the NT-200 predecessor era (operated 1993-1998) up to the first Baikal-GVD cluster; press-account date, day precision not independently confirmed.

intervals.label: Baikal-GVD construction
intervals.quote: In early April, members of the Baikal collaboration deployed and started operation of the first cluster of the Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD).
intervals.note: Ongoing annual cluster deployment; facility continues to expand as of the 2023 status paper (96 strings across multiple clusters in the winter 2023 campaign). Dating of the first cluster: the CERN Courier article of 22 July 2015 reports the first cluster, named Dubna (192 optical modules), deployed in early April 2015 (interval start 2015); the 2023 status paper says the first cluster of the telescope was deployed in 2016 with 288 OMs.

notes: Only one site (the lake deployment point) is modelled here; derived fields (site_ids, accelerator_ids, beamline_ids, institution_id, document_ids, experiment_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

summary.plain: A Russian-led neutrino telescope growing year by year on the bottom of Lake Baikal, the world's deepest freshwater lake. Strings of light sensors hang beneath the ice, watching for flashes made by neutrinos from space.
summary.technical: Baikal-GVD (Gigaton Volume Detector): expanding underwater neutrino telescope in the southern basin of Lake Baikal, operated by INR RAS with international partners; traces to 1980s-era Baikal neutrino experiments (NT-200), first Baikal-GVD cluster deployed 2015, under continuous annual expansion since.
